canh.phat-hien: Each dot records one electron detected at the screen.
canh.mo-ta-nguon: Monochromatic electron beam. Click to detect one more electron.
canh.mo-ta-khe: Slit centers are {0} nm apart. Each slit is 50 nm wide.
canh.mo-ta-doc: Probe at x = {0} mm. Relative density here is {1}.
canh.v: Overlap of the path markers V
canh.chu-thich: The cyan curve shows the predicted density. The dashed curve is the single-slit envelope. Detections are sampled within the screen window from −1.25 to +1.25 mm.
bai.ten: Double slits: building interference fringes one electron at a time
bai.moTa: Watch the dots accumulate on the screen, change the slit separation and try tagging the paths.
bai.yChinh: One electron leaves one dot. After many repetitions with the same preparation, fringes emerge in the density of dots. When the two paths through the slits are indistinguishable, we add their amplitudes before calculating the probability.
bai.giaiThich: The simulation sends a monochromatic electron beam straight towards two identical slits. You can change the wavelength, the slit separation and how well the paths can be distinguished. The screen records individual detections, while the curve shows the predicted distribution. The source, slits and screen are enlarged by different factors. The dimensions are chosen for this numerical experiment.
bai.conSo.1: With a wavelength of **50 pm**, a center-to-center slit separation of **200 nm** and a screen **1 m** away, the fringe period is **0.25 mm** in the small-angle approximation.
bai.conSo.2: For a slit **50 nm** wide, the first zero of the diffraction envelope lies **1 mm** from the center.
bai.hieuDung: It takes many electrons to reveal a fringe pattern. Each electron is recorded at a single position. The model predicts the distribution of these positions without assigning each electron a classical trajectory from source to screen.
bai.nguon: Written by Trí Lữ. R. P. Feynman, R. B. Leighton and M. Sands, The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Vol. III, Chapter 1, §§ 1–4 to 1–7. OpenStax, University Physics, Vol. 3, §§ 4.3 and 6.5. The dimensions are simulation parameters.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.1: Distinguish a single detection from the distribution that builds up over many detections.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.2: Calculate the fringe spacing and the positions of the zeros from the wavelength, slit separation and distance to the screen.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.3: Predict how the distribution changes when a device records which slit the electron passes through.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.1.noiDung:
The source prepares electrons with the same {{bước sóng de Broglie|de Broglie wavelength}}. A barrier with two slits stands in front of the detection screen. Each electron is recorded as **one dot**. A click represents one detection. At high rates the simulation plays only a fraction of the clicks so you can hear them separately.

Out of $N$ detections, suppose $n_j$ land in the small bin numbered $j$. The relative frequency for that bin is $f_j=n_j/N$. We can count the dots exactly and still be unable to tell where the next one will land.

+++ A closer look · What does the picture show?
The slits and screen are enlarged so you can see and drag them. A dot appears at the point of detection. The vertical spread simply separates the marks. This lesson calculates the distribution across the screen horizontally.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Clear the screen and record 1 electron|mot]], then [[Record 1 more electron|them]]. Click a few times and compare the positions.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.ten: From scattered dots to bright bands
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.noiDung:
Leave both slits open and let the source run. At first the dots appear scattered at random. As detections accumulate, dense bands emerge with sparsely populated bands between them. This is {{giao thoa lượng tử|quantum interference}}. Fringes can form even when electrons pass through the apparatus one at a time.

+++ A closer look · Counting fluctuations decrease slowly
If the probability for a bin is $p$ and the trials are independent, the standard deviation of its relative frequency is $\sqrt{p(1-p)/N}$. Quadrupling the number of trials halves the typical fluctuation in relative frequency. Once the screen fills up, it keeps only the most recent marks.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Record rapidly|nhanh]], inspect the dark gaps, then [[Start collecting again|lai]].
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.ten: Close one slit, then reopen it
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.noiDung:
With just one slit of width $a$ open, the distribution on the screen has a high central peak with smaller lobes on either side. This is diffraction through **a single slit of finite width**. For a distant screen at small angles, the distance from the center to the first minimum is $x_0=\lambda L/a$.

+++ A closer look · The envelope and the fine fringes
Let $\beta=\pi ax/(\lambda L)$. The relative detection density for one slit is $(\sin\beta/\beta)^2$, with a limiting value of one at the center. With both slits open, this same factor determines the outer envelope. Each time the setup changes, the screen is cleared so that all the counts come from the same experiment.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Open only one slit|motkhe]], then [[Open both slits|haikhe]]. Compare the spacing between dark regions in the two patterns.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.ten: Why do some positions receive no electrons?
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.noiDung:
At any given point on the screen, each slit contributes a {{biên độ xác suất|probability amplitude}}. If the two alternatives cannot be distinguished, the probability is proportional to $|A_1+A_2|^2$. Equal amplitudes in phase give a large result. When they are half a cycle out of phase, they cancel.

At the initial setting for this step, adjacent bright fringes of the interference factor alone are **0.25 mm** apart. Move right by half that distance to reach the first dark node.

+++ A closer look · Reading the phase with the probe
At small angles the path difference is $\delta\simeq dx/L$ and the phase difference is $\phi=2\pi\delta/\lambda$. At $x=0{,}125\ \mathrm{mm}$, $\delta=\lambda/2$ and $\phi=\pi$. A single open slit would still produce a signal here.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Face the screen|man]]. Drag the yellow probe along the screen and watch the relative density.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.thuThach.de: Drag the probe to the first dark node to the right of center. The tolerance is 0.015 mm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.thuThach.goiY: The probe should be half a fringe spacing from the center of the screen.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.ten: Move the slits and predict the fringe spacing
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.noiDung:
The slit centers are a distance $d$ apart. At small angles the interference factor repeats every $\Delta x=\lambda L/d$. As the slits move farther apart, the same displacement across the screen produces a larger phase difference, so the fringes move closer together.

+++ A closer look · Calculate before you drag
For $L=1\ \mathrm{m}$ and $\lambda=50\ \mathrm{pm}$, increasing $d$ from $200$ to $400\ \mathrm{nm}$ reduces $\Delta x$ from $0{,}25$ to $0{,}125\ \mathrm{mm}$. The peaks can shift slightly under the envelope. The formula gives the period of the interference factor.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[View the whole apparatus|toan]]. Drag the green knob on the barrier to move the two slits symmetrically.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.thuThach.de: Keep the wavelength at 50 pm and drag the slits until the fringe spacing is 0.125 mm, with an error of less than 0.006 mm.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.thuThach.goiY: To halve the fringe spacing, double the distance between the slit centers.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.noiDung:
The electron’s wavelength is related to its momentum by $\lambda=h/p$. Increasing the momentum shortens the wavelength. If the dimensions of the apparatus stay fixed, the fringe spacing also decreases.

+++ A closer look · Two changes that are easy to confuse
Increasing the slit separation brings the fine fringes closer together. Reducing the wavelength shrinks **both the fringe spacing and the width of the central diffraction peak**. For the initial settings in this step, reducing the wavelength from 50 to 25 pm changes the fringe spacing from 0.25 to 0.125 mm and moves the first zero of the envelope from 1 to 0.5 mm.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Double the momentum|nhan]], then [[Return to 50 pm|goc]]. Compare the two envelopes before and after the change.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.ten: When the apparatus records the path
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.noiDung:
Suppose a marker associates two different states with the two paths. If these tags are perfectly distinguishable, detections at the same point on the screen can still be accompanied by different marker states. When we add up the screen counts, the interference term disappears. Nobody needs to read the stored tag.

+++ A closer look · How much the marker states overlap
For equally illuminated slits, the factor $V$ is the magnitude of the overlap between the two marker states. The distribution takes the form $P(x)\propto(\sin\beta/\beta)^2[1+V\cos\phi]$. Identical tags give $V=1$, while orthogonal tags give $V=0$. In both limiting cases, the single-slit diffraction envelope remains.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Fully tag the paths|danh]], then [[Remove the path distinction before emitting more electrons|bo]]. Drag the probe to examine a region that used to contain a dark node.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.thuThach.de: Make the two markers perfectly distinguishable, then drag the probe to the old dark node 0.125 mm to the right of center (tolerance 0.015 mm).
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.thuThach.goiY: At V = 0, this position fills in. Place the probe at the original coordinate.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.noiDung:
Examine the detection marks before revealing the predicted curve. If $L$ is known, the spacing of the bands reveals the ratio $\lambda/d$. Their contrast shows how strongly the two paths can still interfere.

+++ A closer look · What does it take to identify the cause?
In this experiment you can vary one parameter at a time. In the laboratory, fringes can also blur if the source contains several wavelengths or the apparatus vibrates. To attribute a change to path marking, keep the other conditions stable and compare many detections.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Show only the dots|giau]] and predict the positions of the peaks. Then [[Compare with the theoretical curve|hien]].
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.1.y: Higher momentum gives a shorter wavelength.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.2.y: Applies when the two paths cannot be distinguished.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.3.y: The slits are separated by d and the screen is a distance L away. Use this for a distant screen and small angles.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.4.y: Here a is the width of one rectangular slit.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.hoi: Turn the source down until only one electron is in the apparatus at a time. After many emissions, what pattern does the screen show?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.chon.1: Individual dots accumulate to form fringes
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.chon.2: Each electron draws a whole fringe by itself
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.chon.3: Just two lines directly behind the slits
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.giai: The probability for an individual detection depends on the sum of the two amplitudes. The separate detections sample that same distribution.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.hoi: Keep the wavelength and screen distance fixed and double the slit separation. What happens to the fringe period?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.giai: Fringe spacing is inversely proportional to slit separation.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.hoi: At a dark node of the two-slit pattern, electrons can still arrive when either slit is open by itself. What cancels when both slits are open?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.giai: Amplitudes have phase. When two amplitudes have the same magnitude and opposite phases, their sum has squared magnitude zero.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.hoi: Both slits remain open, but the two paths leave orthogonal marker states. What pattern remains?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.chon.1: A distribution following the diffraction envelope
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.chon.2: Fringes just as clear as before
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.giai: When the marker state is ignored, we add the probabilities contributed by the two paths. Each slit still produces diffraction.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.hoi: Doubling d and halving λ both reduce the fringe spacing by half. What other feature lets you tell which change occurred?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.dap: Compare the widths of the diffraction envelopes. With a and L fixed, the envelope zeros depend only on λ. Reducing λ narrows the entire envelope, while changing d leaves its width unchanged.

bai.baiGiang.docThem.2: OpenStax, University Physics, Vol. 3, § 4.3 (two slits of finite width) and § 6.5 (matter waves).
bai.baiGiang.thuatNgu.1.nghia: A complex quantity whose squared magnitude gives the predicted probability.
bai.baiGiang.thuatNgu.2.nghia: The enhancement or suppression of probability when amplitudes for indistinguishable alternatives are added.
bai.baiGiang.thuatNgu.3.nghia: The wavelength associated with a particle of momentum p through λ = h/p.
bai.baiGiang.thuatNgu.4.nghia: A physical record that can distinguish which slit an electron passed through.
